subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard browser receive only configured shared gateway auth, or may it reuse native/stored device tokens for parity with native clients?
rationale: Two open same-surface PRs implement conflicting credential policies, and the choice affects both security boundary and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Rebase this PR, cover show, fast path, and endpoint reload with shared-token-only injection, then require macOS proof before merge.

options.title: Allow native-token browser parity
options.body: Close or replace this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction after documenting why native device tokens are safe for browser injection.

options.title: Hold both auth PRs
options.body: Pause both drafts until a maintainer writes the Dashboard auth policy and expected upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Rebase this PR, cover show, fast path, and endpoint reload with shared-token-only injection, then require macOS proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and recently changed the Dashboard auth/reload surface now blocking this PR.
